outline: Scientific visualization is the use of computer graphics to visually represent the composite meaning of the large amount of data obtained by scientific computation, extensive monitoring, or engineering experiments. The scientific visualization in this semester focuses on the advanced C/C++ programming skills and computer vision, visualization, and practical applications.
schedule:
Week 1: Introduction to Computer Vision and Visualization
Week 2: Installation of C++ Development with Qt and OpenCV
Week 3: Graphical User Interface Development using C++/Qt (I)
Week 4: Graphical User Interface Development using C++/Qt (II) with OpenCV
Week 5: Documentation
Week 6: Version Control and Maintenance
Week 7: 2D Coordinate Transformation (I): Theory and formula
Week 8: 2D Coordinate Transformation (II): C/C++ Programming Exercises
Week 9: Midterm: Rapid Programming and Documentation
Week 10: 3D Coordinate Transformation (I): Theory and Formula
Week 11: 3D Coordinate Transformation (II): Camera Model
Week 12: 3D Coordinate Transformation (III): C/C++ Programming Exercises
Week 13: Camera Calibration
Week 14: Machine Learning Basics
Week 15: Machine Learning Exercises
Week 16: Final Project Opening Discussion (I)
Week 17: Final Project Opening Discussion (II)
Week 18: Final Project Presentations
assessment:
1. Lecture activities (attendance, interaction, lecture assistance) (30% +/- 5%)
2. Midterm (20% +/- 5%)
3: Final Presentation (20% +/- 5%)
4: Final Report (30% +/- 5%)
